subject: On-prem private endpoint — egress boundary & allowlist questions
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
To: lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Data-plane egress expectations for on-prem private endpoint

Lukas —

Thanks for taking this. We're standing up Redwood's private endpoint inside our on-prem VPC and the security team has two critical asks before we can approve networking:

1) An explicit, stable list of outbound IP addresses (or small CIDR ranges) that the private endpoint will use to reach Redwood control-plane services, health checks, and metric sinks. We need this for our perimeter firewall allowlisting.
2) Clarify which external destinations are required (e.g., telemetry/metrics, KMS, CRL/OCSP) and whether TLS SNI or certificate pinning is sufficient instead of IPs for some flows.

We prefer IPs where possible due to our segmentation rules, but we understand cloud egress ranges can change. If you have a recommended topology (e.g., NAT through a static egress proxy we host, or you host a static egress gateway) that would be great to see.

Also, can you flag any endpoints that must be reachable on non-standard ports or where mTLS is required?

Appreciate a short runbook and an initial allowlist CSV so our networking team can do the ACL change window.

Thanks,
Tom
Infrastructure Security
Acme Health

Tom —

Thanks — good questions. High level summary first, then an action list and a small ask from your ops team: 

Summary (short):
- Redwood private endpoint (control-plane + runtime control APIs) requires outbound TCP to a handful of stable IPs we publish. These are used for control RPCs, metrics, and configuration fetches.
- TLS is used for all control-plane communication; mTLS is optional for customers who enable our Private+HSM KMS integration.
- For customers who cannot allow large public ranges, we support a model where we allocate a static egress IP pair for your deployment and announce only those (recommended).

Action items we will deliver:
1) CSV with recommended allowlist: control-plane IPs + explained ports (attached draft).
2) Firewall rule-naming suggestions and sample iptables/ACL fragments.
3) A short rollback/maintenance window procedure.

Questions for you:
- Do you have a preferred approach: (A) Accept our published IP block and periodic updates, (B) Request Redwood-reserved static egress IPs for your tenant, or (C) NAT all traffic through an Acme-managed proxy (we'll provide FQDNs and SNI guidance)?
- Any constraints around DNS resolution (split-horizon) or egress through a corporate proxy?

Attaching a first-pass allowlist (CSV) and a 1-page rule-set. These are drafts — we'll finalize after your feedback.

Cheers,

Lukas Meyer
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fw: Firewall ruleset draft + port breakdown (Redwood private endpoint)

Tom —

Forwarding a slightly expanded rule-set and an annotated PDF with rationale for each port. Key calls-out:

- Control-plane API: TCP 443 outbound to our control-plane IPs (listed in the CSV). TLS required.
- Metrics/telemetry: TCP 443 outbound to metrics.redwood-inference.com; optional to switch to a customer-pushed metrics endpoint if you need to keep all traffic inside your network.
- Model artifact fetches (initial model pulls): TCP 443 outbound to model-storage.redwood-inference.com; large binaries — allow for several minutes of egress during first model bootstrap.
- CRL/OCSP: Standard HTTPS (443) to public CAs; if your environment blocks general internet egress, we can provide a CRL mirror endpoint.
- KMS/HSM: If you use Redwood-managed KMS, we will make outbound connections to our KMS control plane on 443. If you use a customer-managed HSM behind your firewall, we will not reach out to public KMS endpoints.

Attachments: fw-ruleset-draft-Redwood-v1.pdf (contains ACL snippets: Palo Alto / Cisco ASA / iptables), acme-egress-ips-20270407.csv (updated)

Let me know if you want us to convert the ACLs into your firewall vendor format; we can do that as a follow-up.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Solutions — Networking
Redwood Inference

Team / Tom —

Two security items I want on record for Acme's approval flow (SOC2/third-party audit needs):

1) Change notification and CIDR churn tolerance: If Redwood republishes or grows any public IP blocks that are in the allowlist, we need an automated notice (email + webhook) at least 14 days ahead and a documented method for emergency-IP rotations with a clear rollback.

2) Observability & logging: The private endpoint must be able to push connection logs and TLS fingerprints to a tenant-controlled logging destination or to Redwood with tenant-level separation. For Acme we recommend tenant-only S3-compatible bucket or your SIEM ingestion endpoint; if you require that to be over mTLS, specify certs and we'll integrate.

Acceptance criteria (minimal):
- Static egress pair allocated OR an agreed notification cadence for IP churn.
- ACL fragment and test plan executed in a staging window (we need evidence: pcap or connection logs showing handshake to control-plane IPs).
- Telemetry ingestion endpoint confirmed (URL + port + auth method).

If those are OK I can sign off on the security checklist and we can schedule the production firewall change window.

Mina Haddad
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
